t.1.62.1: Janamejaya said: O brahmin, I have heard from you in full this account of the descent through partial incarnations of the gods, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, and likewise of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.
t.1.62.3: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was a valiant man named Duḥṣanta, the founder of the lineage of the Pauravas, the protector of the earth bounded by the four seas, O best of the Bharatas.
t.1.62.2: But I wish once more, O brahmin, to have this lineage of the Kurus told by you from its beginning, in the presence of the hosts of brahmin seers.
t.1.62.4: That lord of men enjoyed the whole earth in all its four quarters; that victor in battle ruled even the lands bounded by the sea.
t.1.62.5: That crusher of foes enjoys dominion over all the lands, reaching even to the barbarian forest tribes, lands bounded by the ocean, that mine of jewels, and filled with people of the four classes.
t.1.62.7: At that time, O tiger among men, while that lord of the land ruled, men pursued righteous pleasure and attained both dharma and wealth.
t.1.62.8: While he was lord of the land, my son, there was no fear of thieves, not even the slightest fear of hunger, nor was there any fear of disease.
t.1.62.6: While that king ruled, there was no one who caused a mixing of the social classes, no person who failed to till the soil or failed to pay tribute, and no evildoer at all.
t.1.62.10: Then the rain-god Parjanya poured rain in due season, the crops were laden with fruit, and the wealth-bearing earth was rich with every kind of jewel.
t.1.62.9: The classes took delight in their own duties, free of craving in their rites to the gods; and relying on that protector of the earth, they lived without fear from any quarter.
t.1.62.11: That youth, of wondrous and mighty valor, with a frame as hard as the thunderbolt, could lift Mount Mandara with his arms and carry it off together with its woods and groves.
t.1.62.12: He became thoroughly accomplished in the bow, in fighting with the mace, and in weapons wielded by the hilt, as well as in riding on the back of an elephant and on the back of a horse.
t.1.62.13: In strength he was equal to Viṣṇu, and in splendour like the sun; in imperturbability he was like the ocean, and in forbearance like the earth.
t.1.62.14: Esteemed by all, that lord of the earth, whose city and kingdom were content, dwelt moreover among a people renowned for their dispositions devoted to dharma.
